runs.name: opens-on-a-plan
runs.title: The app opens on a drawn plan
runs.summary:
You asked to review the floor-plan drawing and report whether each listed feature was present.
The drawing was visible and not empty: it showed a dashed plot boundary, a building within it, and at least three rooms separated by walls.
Held: A north point marked “N” and a scale bar marked “0” and “2 m” were visible.
Held: The ground-floor plan included a staircase with parallel tread lines and an arrow indicating the direction of rise.
Held: At least one door showed both a quarter-circle swing arc and a straight leaf line.
Held: Every room had a name and an area shown in square metres.
Final result: all five requested assertions held.

runs.name: audit-plan-walkability
runs.summary:
The test treated a required inspection result as something that had to be true. The ground-floor findings explicitly report that the staircase has no door, so the combined checkpoint could not pass for this intentionally invalid plan.
Change the final check to record whether the stair door is present and report the finding. Do not assert that every inspected plan must have a stair door when the fixture is designed to expose missing-door findings.
